title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Cote 140-3 continues the 'Longue Marche' study of the 'équation des lacets'. This is the analysis of Galois-type automorphism groups of profinite SL2(Z)/PSL2(Z) and the modular tower, the setting that later became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme. ρ0 and σ0 are the standard torsion generators: in SL2 they have orders 6 and 4. The previous page records L_ρ ≅ Z/6 and L_σ ≅ Z/4, the cyclic subgroups they generate. M is a group of (outer) automorphism data. Γ0 = Γ^~_{Q,*} is the base group over which everything is fibred; the maps to Γ0 are presumably arithmetic/cyclotomic characters. M^! is a distinguished subgroup of M. M^? is an extension of M with kernel μ_ρ, defined on p. 626' as a fibre-product subgroup.

This page.
(1) Recall (122): M^? = N^?_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0} Z^!_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M, with the notation of (123):
- N_{ρ0} = Norm_M(L_{ρ0}) and N_{σ0} = Norm_M(L_{σ0});
- Z_{σ0} = Centr_M(L_{σ0}) = Centr_M(σ0);
- Z^!_{σ0} = Z_{σ0} ∩ M^!. Grothendieck notes this also equals N_{σ0} ∩ M^!, i.e. elements of M^! that normalize L_{σ0} automatically centralize it, because M^! acts trivially through the character (Z/4)^*;
- N^?_{ρ0} = Z^!_{ρ0}·μ_{τ'} ⊂ N_{ρ0}, with Z^!_{ρ0} = Z_{ρ0} ∩ M^!.
Hence M^? ⊂ N_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0} N_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M, which is the big group M^{(♮')}_{ρ0,σ0} of the previous page.
(2) Define (124): M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} := M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} ∩ M^?, the intersection taken inside that triple fibre product. A margin note says this is independent of an auxiliary choice. Grothendieck crosses out an attempted product formula N^? ×_{Γ0} N^! ×_{Γ0} M^♮; the corrected version reappears as (127) on the next page.
(3) Consider the commutative square (119)/(125): M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮ over M^? → M.

Purpose (next page). Since M^? → M has kernel μ_ρ, and μ_ρ ⊂ M^♮_{ρ0,σ0}, one gets an exact sequence 1 → μ_ρ → M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮. A lemma then shows the last map is onto. This carries out the programme announced on p. 646: cut inside M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} a smaller group that is an extension of M^♮ by μ (not by the larger Z/6 × Z/4 kernel). The goal is a minimal extension of the 'natural' automorphism group by roots of unity, built from normalizers and centralizers of the elliptic torsion.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The crossed-out attempt to write M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} directly as N^? ×_{Γ0} N^! ×_{Γ0} M^♮ is abandoned on this page and corrected on the next page as (127)/(128).
Minor slip in the image: the displayed inclusion M^? ⊂ N_{ρ0} ×_{ρ0} N_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M has the first fibre-product subscript written as ρ0 instead of Γ0.
The equality Z_{σ0} ∩ M^! = N_{σ0} ∩ M^! is asserted without proof on this page. It holds provided M^! acts trivially on Aut(L_{σ0}) ≅ (Z/4)^*, which is presumably how M^! is defined.

ideas.what: Fibre-product description of the extension M^? of M by μ_ρ, using the normalizer/centralizer subgroups of the torsion cyclic subgroups L_ρ and L_σ, fibred over Γ0
ideas.modern_name: Pullback (fibre product) of groups over a Galois-type quotient; extensions of automorphism groups of the profinite modular group by roots of unity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; the general GT context is due to Grothendieck (Esquisse), Drinfeld and Ihara
ideas.where_published: Second part of La Longue Marche (unpublished); the published Malgoire edition covers only part of the manuscript

ideas.what: Defining a smaller group M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} = M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} ∩ M^? so that it maps onto M^♮ with kernel μ_ρ
ideas.modern_name: Intersection of subgroups in a fibre product to obtain a minimal extension

ideas.what: Observation that elements of M^! normalizing L_σ automatically centralize it
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer equals centralizer under trivial action on the automorphism character of a cyclic subgroup

deep.surprise_reason: This is internal bookkeeping in a long unpublished computation: it recalls definitions and intersects subgroups inside a fibre product to build a minimal μ-extension. The broader project (Galois action on profinite SL2(Z), loop equations) is known in outline. Nothing on this page appears to be a self-contained new result or an unexploited connection.
transcription_corrections: The decoration transcribed as '⊊' / '\Subset^{\subsetneq}' on M_{ρ0,σ0} and M is Grothendieck's hooked symbol, written ♮ on the neighbouring pages. Read M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0}, M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} and M^♮.
The third line of (123) defines Z^!_{σ0} = Z_{σ0} ∩ M^! (an overwritten letter replaces a crossed-out Z_{ρ0}), not N^!_{σ0}. This matches the Z^!_{σ0} used in (122).
In (122) the first factor should read N^?_{ρ0} (subscript ρ0).
In the second line of (123) the centralizer should read Z_{σ0} = Centr_M(L_{σ0}) = Centr_M(σ0).
The margin note reads approximately 'indépendamment du choix d'un ♮G' (or similar). It refers to independence from a choice, not a set-theoretic symbol.
The inclusion line is written in the image as N_{ρ0} ×_{ρ0} N_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M; the intended form is N_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0} N_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M.
The crossed-out line under (124) reads approximately '= N^?_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0} N^!_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M^♮'.
